entries.proposition: DESIGN: a narrative review; the central experimental claim (dexmedetomidine produces an absence-status-like state in WAG/Rij rats) is the author group own work, cited as its refs 49 and 65.
entries.snippet: Our team recently investigated the alpha2-adrenergic modulation of spike–wave epilepsy in symptomatic WAG/Rij rats using systemic injections of dexmedetomidine

entries.proposition: SIGN: alpha2 agonists increase spike-wave activity in genetically prone rats; antagonists suppress it. The direction of an adrenergic manipulation on seizures therefore depends on receptor subtype and site, and the same review notes that presynaptic alpha2 activation lowers noradrenaline release.
entries.snippet: Antagonists of alpha2-ARs, in contrast, suppress SWDs (Table 1) putatively via an indirect effect on vigilance

entries.proposition: DOSE: the absence-status state is produced by low doses; a very high dose reverses the effect (a decrease in SWDs and deep sedation), so the dose-response is non-monotonic.
entries.snippet: Low doses of dexmedetomidine caused a pro-absence effect in rats, whereas high doses caused a reduction in SWDs and deep sedation

entries.proposition: The absence-status duration was not dose-dependent and was predetermined by baseline seizure intensity: the response is a property of the seizure phenotype, not of the dose.
entries.snippet: the duration of EEG-behavioral correlates of absence status was not dose-dependent and was predetermined by the intensity of absence seizures at baseline

entries.proposition: In healthy control rats alpha2 agonists did not induce spike-wave seizures; the authors attribute it, speculatively, to a different alpha2 receptor distribution (thalamic alpha2B overexpression in epileptic rats), which is untested.
entries.snippet: Alpha2-AR agonists did not induce spike–wave seizures in healthy control rats (49) probably because the receptor-binding profile

entries.proposition: INTERNAL TENSION: the limitations say absence status was only found in rats with spontaneous seizures at baseline, while the conclusion says agonists induced seizures in subclinical individuals without prior seizures and could unmask hidden absence epilepsy in humans.
entries.snippet: Absence status was only found in epileptic rats with spontaneous absence seizures at baseline (49).

entries.proposition: The conclusion extends the rat result to clinical use: dexmedetomidine and other alpha2 agonists could help identify hidden forms of absence epilepsy; no human datum is given.
entries.snippet: dexmedetomidine, which is frequently used in clinical practice, and other alpha2-adrenoreceptor agonists could help identify hidden forms of absence epilepsy

entries.proposition: The authors state the translational value of the model is at an early stage and that pharmacological provocation is the major limitation.
entries.snippet: The translational value of the proposed model is still in its early stages and needs more extensive ex- and pre-clinical research

entries.proposition: Figure 1 is a schematic: sleep-wake continuum with spike-wave discharges during drowsiness and light slow-wave sleep, target 1 presynaptic alpha2 receptor in the locus coeruleus (noradrenaline down), target 2 postsynaptic thalamic alpha2B receptor; it carries one example EEG trace and one photograph, no measurement.
